name: Blake Hall
profile: Former US Army Ranger and Harvard MBA who co-founded ID.me in 2010 (originally TroopSwap, a military deals site) with fellow Ranger Matt Thompson; renamed ID.me in 2013, it became a leading digital identity-verification network used by federal and state agencies and companies, valued around $2B. He remains CEO and a frequent voice on identity fraud policy.
interesting_fact: As a battalion reconnaissance platoon leader in Iraq he led some 450 combat patrols with no casualties in his platoon and received two Bronze Star medals before leaving the Army in 2008.
deep_cut_fact: He applied to Harvard Business School on his battalion commander's push; Hall recalled deciding to 'apply to the best of the best if I'm going to do this.' ID.me began life as TroopSwap, a Groupon-style deals site for service members.

public_contacts.value: ID.mePR@rhstrategic.com (Raffetto Herman Strategic Communications, listed in 2022 release)

notes: Comfortable with media and podcasts (veteran-entrepreneur story). PR agency contact is from a 2022 release and may be outdated; check ID.me's newsroom for current press contact.

name: Etai Hochman
current_role: Co-founder of At-Bay (former CTO); co-founder and CTO of Mirato, acquired by Sayari in July 2025 (current title post-acquisition unconfirmed)
profile: Israeli engineer who co-founded cyber insurer At-Bay in 2016 with Rotem Iram and Roman Itskovich, serving as its first CTO; At-Bay pairs insurance with active security monitoring and reached unicorn status. He then co-founded Mirato (2018), an AI third-party risk management platform, with Aki Eldar; Mirato raised a $9M seed in 2021 and was bought by US risk-intelligence firm Sayari in 2025.
interesting_fact: He has built two companies in adjacent risk markets: At-Bay (cyber insurance + security monitoring) and Mirato, whose 'Risk Hunter' tool models how risk propagates across a company's supply chain; Mirato was acquired by Sayari in July 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Mirato's $9M 2021 seed round was led by Dov Moran's Grove Ventures (Moran invented the USB flash drive) with American Express Ventures participating, and Hochman was named CTO alongside CEO Aki Eldar, ex-CEO of Microsoft-acquired Secure Islands.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal social/website found. No longer operational at At-Bay (board observer/advisor per profiles). Current role at Sayari after the Mirato acquisition not confirmed. Education details (Bar-Ilan math, TAU MBA) only from aggregator profiles.

name: Krishna Depura
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Mindtickle (San Francisco / Pune)
profile: Indian-born engineer and ISB MBA (Class of 2006) who co-founded Mindtickle in 2011 with former PubMatic colleagues Deepak Diwakar and Nishant Mungali. Mindtickle grew from a gamified employee-learning tool into a revenue-enablement and sales-readiness platform, valued at over $1B; he leads it as CEO, now pushing AI coaching and role-play products.
interesting_fact: Before Mindtickle he spent about five years at startups building photonic and semiconductor chips, then worked at Infinera, Microsoft (program manager) and ad-tech firm PubMatic (Director of Products until 2010).
deep_cut_fact: In a 2012 ISB alumni profile he said Mindtickle came 'after ten years of trying, failing and learning,' wished he'd started his entrepreneurial journey during his ISB days, and named his fondest ISB memory as alumni worldwide making the 'world's first wiki movie' Sapney.
notes: Also writes occasional TechCrunch contributor pieces (techcrunch.com/author/krishna-depura). Personal interests per ISB profile: travel and water sports.

name: Jacob Boudreau
profile: Co-founded Atlanta-based Stord in 2015 with CEO Sean Henry out of Georgia Tech's CREATE-X student incubator; Stord started as a peer-to-peer storage idea and pivoted into an on-demand warehousing network and now a 'cloud supply chain' (fulfillment, OMS, software) for consumer brands. A 2025 Series F valued it around $3B. Boudreau leads technology as CTO.
interesting_fact: Stord came out of Georgia Tech's CREATE-X student startup program, and Atlanta security entrepreneur Chris Klaus (ISS founder), who backs CREATE-X, became one of Stord's early investors; Henry met him at Georgia Tech.
deep_cut_fact: Boudreau and Henry were named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2018, then picked as 'All-Star Alumni' on the 2020 Manufacturing & Industry list, which recognizes those 'creating the products, methods and materials of tomorrow.'
notes: Low-profile technical co-founder; CEO Sean Henry is the public face. Recent Stord releases (2025-26) list David Packman as media contact.

name: Shay Cohen
current_role: Co-founder and VP Engineering, Fabric (formerly CommonSense Robotics), Tel Aviv
profile: Israeli engineer and former IDF lieutenant colonel who co-founded Fabric (founded 2015 as CommonSense Robotics) with Elram Goren and Ori Avraham. Fabric builds compact robotic micro-fulfillment centers that let retailers run fast, profitable on-demand and grocery delivery inside cities; it reached a ~$1B valuation. Cohen leads hardware, manufacturing and deployment.
interesting_fact: CommonSense built the world's first underground automated warehouse, in the -1 parking level of Tel Aviv's Shalom Meir Tower (the city's oldest skyscraper), to serve one-hour grocery deliveries from under-used urban real estate (2019).
deep_cut_fact: Before Fabric he served as a Lieutenant Colonel in the IDF Intelligence Technology Unit, received the Israel Defense Prize for leading complex multidisciplinary systems, and holds a BSc in mechanical engineering from Ben-Gurion University and an MSc in biomechanics from the University of Delaware.

public_contacts.value: joseph@headline.media (Joseph Moses, Headline Media, listed as Fabric/CommonSense media contact, 2019)

name: Prajit Nanu
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Nium (leads the company from its San Francisco office)
profile: Indian-born fintech founder who co-founded Instarem in 2014 with Michael Bermingham as a consumer remittance app in Singapore; it rebranded as Nium in 2019 and became a B2B cross-border payments infrastructure provider, reaching unicorn status in 2021 (~$2B valuation in 2022). Nium says it holds licenses in 40+ markets and processes $60B+ a year; Nanu is now pushing stablecoin settlement and a planned US IPO.
interesting_fact: He started the company after personally experiencing the friction of sending money across borders; Nium now connects 190+ countries and issues 41M+ card tokens a year, and recently added USDC stablecoin funding and settlement via a Circle partnership.
deep_cut_fact: In September 2026 Nanu was named to Skift's 2026 Power Rankings of travel-industry leaders (travel is one of Nium's biggest verticals), and he has been an EY Entrepreneur Of The Year finalist.
notes: Media-friendly CEO who speaks regularly on payments, stablecoins and AI; press@nium.com is the published PR route. Relocated leadership to San Francisco ahead of US IPO plans (IPO target slipped to end-2026 per 2024 reports).

current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Oura Health (left the company in 2020); current role not confirmed
profile: Finnish engineer from Oulu who co-founded Oura Health in 2013 with fellow engineers and researchers (ex-Nokia/Polar backgrounds) to build a sensor-packed smart ring tracking sleep, heart rate and temperature. name: Hideki Yoshino
current_role: Founder and CEO, Clean Planet Inc. (Tokyo)
profile: Japanese serial entrepreneur who founded Clean Planet (2012), which develops 'Quantum Hydrogen Energy' (QHe) - a heat source using nano-materials and hydrogen that it says produces energy without fossil fuels or nuclear fission - working with Tohoku University scientists; it has been valued around $1B. Earlier he founded and ran GABA Corporation, the 1-on-1 English school chain, from 1995 to 2004.

deep_cut_fact: Before clean energy he built an English-education business: he founded GABA, the one-on-one English conversation school, and was CEO 1995-2004; he holds a BA in Law from the University of Tokyo and an MSc in Finance from London Business School.
notes: Highly relevant to an energy podcast (novel hydrogen/condensed-matter heat technology). Active public speaker - e.g. spoke on 'Co-Creating Next-Generation Energy' at the 52nd Japan-New Zealand Business Conference in Sendai on 2 Nov 2026. Clean Planet raised further capital from 77 Capital in Oct 2026. Company claims about QHe are its own; treat scientific claims cautiously.
